name: Kaga Toshiba 300 mm power semiconductor fab

parties.name: Kaga Toshiba Electronics
parties.note: Toshiba's main discrete semiconductor production subsidiary.

parties.name: Toshiba Electronic Devices & Storage Corporation
parties.note: Parent company that announced and is investing in the fab.

parties.name: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (Japan)
parties.note: Recognized the ROHM and Toshiba power device plan in December 2023 with a subsidy of up to one third of the joint investment; Toshiba expects the grant to cover part of its equipment spending.

summary: A new 300 mm wafer fab for silicon power semiconductors, mainly MOSFETs and IGBTs, at Kaga Toshiba Electronics in Nomi, Ishikawa Prefecture. Toshiba announced it in February 2022 as a building to be built in two phases, began construction in April 2023 and held the completion ceremony for the first-phase building in May 2024. Mass production began in February 2025. At full first-phase operation Toshiba expects 2.5 times its fiscal 2021 power semiconductor capacity, measured in 200 mm equivalents; the timing of the second phase depends on market conditions. The fab is part of a joint ROHM and Toshiba plan certified for subsidy by Japan's industry ministry.

metrics.note: Toshiba Electronic Devices & Storage and Kaga Toshiba's share of the joint plan with ROHM, for silicon power devices at Kaga Toshiba.
Maximum METI subsidy, one third of the ¥388.3 billion joint plan that covers this fab and the LAPIS Semiconductor Miyazaki Plant No. 2 silicon carbide site.

milestones.note: At announcement, construction was planned to start in spring 2023 and finish in spring 2024.
Completion ceremony for the fab and an office building; equipment installation followed.

notes: Toshiba says construction and start-up of the second phase will be decided according to market trends; no date has been given, so the record is partly operating. Toshiba had already begun 300 mm power production on a line in Kaga Toshiba's existing buildings in the second half of fiscal 2022; that line is not part of this record.
